statutory_dues.text:
i.In respect of statutory dues:
 
(a)In our opinion, the Company has generally been regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues, including Goods and Services tax, Provident Fund, Employees’ State Insurance, Income Tax, Cess and other material statutory dues applicable to it with the appropriate authorities.
 
There were no undisputed amounts payable in respect of Goods and Service tax, Provident Fund, Employees’ State Insurance, Income Tax, Cess and other material statutory dues in arrears as at 31 March 2025 for a period of more than six months from the date they became payable.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The company received a demand of Rs. 1,21,11,680 from the Assessing Officer for the financial year 2016-17, vide dated April 9, 2019. The Commissioner of Income Tax dismissed the Assessing Officer's order, leading to an appeal by the Department to the Tribunal. However, the Tribunal struck down the appeal on 27.08.2021. Subsequently on April 11, 2022, the Principal Commissioner of Income Tax-2, Hyderabad, submitted an appeal to the Telangana High Court.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: (Pr. Commissioner of Income Tax) Income Tax Department, Hyderabad

Promoter group disclosed holding 2.22 Cr shares as of March 31, 2026, with no new encumbrances.
Kapston Services reported Q4FY26 results with revenue growth of 16.7% YoY and announced entry into B2C home services through new subsidiary
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹225.37 Cr (+7.0% YoY), net profit ₹8.41 Cr (+19.1% YoY).
